questions.question: In what time will ₹3720 amount to ₹5282.4 at the rate of 12% per annual simple interest? 12%
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest first. 
SI = 5282.4 − 3720 = ₹1562.4 
 Step 2   Now solve for the time. 
t = 1562.4 × 100 / (3720 × 12) = 3½ years

questions.question: A sum doubles in seven years at simple interest. In how many years will the sum become five times the original sum?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Doubling in 7 years tells you what one 
block is worth. 
P → 2P in 7 yr   ⇒  interest of one 7-year block 
= P 
 Step 2   Five times the sum needs four such 
blocks. 
5P − P = 4P of interest   ⇒  4 blocks = 4 × 7 = 28 
years

questions.question: If the simple interest for 9 years be equal to 45% of the principal, then the rate of interest per annum is equal to:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write it out. 
P × 9 × r / 100 = 45P / 100 
 Step 2   Cancel and solve. 
9r = 45   ∴  r = 5%

questions.question: If the ratio of principal and the simple interest for 5 years is 10 : 7, then the rate of interest (per annum) is:

P : I = 10 : 7   ⇒  I / P = 7/10 
 Step 2   Set it equal to r × t / 100. 
7/10 = r × 5 / 100   ∴  r = 14%

questions.question: The simple interest on ₹2460 will be 162 less than the interest on ₹3000 at the rate of 5% per annum. Find the time taken in years. ₹2460
questions.solution:
Step 1   One calculation on the difference. 
(3000 − 2460) × 5 × t / 100 = 162 
 Step 2   Solve. 
540 × 5 × t / 100 = 27t = 162   ∴  t = 6 years

questions.question: A sum of money becomes 8/7 of itself in 2 years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the annual interest rate.
questions.solution:
Step 1   Read the interest as a fraction of P. 
I / P = (8 − 7) / 7 = 1/7   over 2 years 
 Step 2   Divide by the time, then convert to a 
percentage. 
per year = 1/14   ⇒  R = (1/14) × 100 = 50/7 = 71/7 
%

questions.question: What is the ratio of the simple interest earned on a certain sum of money at 21% per annum for 8 years to that earned on the same sum at the same rate for 21 years?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the two interests and cancel. 
(P × 21 × 8) : (P × 21 × 21)  — P and 21 cancel 
 Step 2   Read the ratio. 
= 8 : 21

questions.question: A person deposited ₹15600 in a fixed deposit at 10% per annum simple interest. After every second year he adds the interest earned to the principal. The interest at the end of 4 years is..
questions.solution:
Step 1   First block, principal ₹15,600. 
10% of 15,600 = ₹1,560 a year   ⇒  2 years = 
₹3,120 
 Step 2   Add it in; the principal changes once. 
new principal = 15,600 + 3,120 = ₹18,720 
 Step 3   Second block on the new principal. 
10% of 18,720 = ₹1,872 a year   ⇒  2 years = 
₹3,744 
 Step 4   Total interest over the 4 years. 
3,120 + 3,744 = ₹6,864

questions.question: A sum of ₹x is lent out in three parts. The first part is lent at 6% per annum at simple interest for 6 years. The second part is lent at 8% per annum for 5 years. And the third part is lent at 12% per annum for 3 years. If all three simple interests are equal, what is the ratio of the three parts? ₹x
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the equality. 
p × 6 × 6 = q × 8 × 5 = r × 12 × 3    ⇒   36p = 40q = 
36r 
 Step 2   Divide right through by the LCM 360. 
p : q : r = 360/36 : 360/40 : 360/36 = 10 : 9 : 10

questions.question: A sum of ₹18,000 is invested for 16 months at 12% per annum at simple interest. What is the total amount after the period? ₹18,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Interest for the period. 
SI = 18,000 × 12 × (16/12) / 100 = ₹2,880 
 Step 2   Amount = principal + interest. 
18,000 + 2,880 = ₹20,880

questions.question: A sum of ₹10000 is deposited in a bank. After one year, another sum of ₹5000 is deposited. After another year the bank pays simple interest at 5% per annum. What is the total amount at the end of 3 years from the time of first deposit? ₹10000
questions.solution:
Step 1   The first deposit runs the full 3 years. 
10,000 × 5 × 3 / 100 = ₹1,500 
 Step 2   The second one joins a year later, so 2 
years. 
5,000 × 5 × 2 / 100 = ₹500 
 Step 3   Add both deposits and both interests. 
15,000 + 2,000 = ₹17,000

questions.question: The difference between the simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 3 years and that at 8% for 3 years is ₹72. The sum is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Convert both. 
10% × 3 = 30% of P        8% × 3 = 24% of P 
 Step 2   The gap is the given ₹72. 
(30 − 24)% of P = 6% of P = 72   ∴  P = ₹1,200

questions.question: The principal, which will give simple interest of ₹4,800 in 4 years at the rate of 16% per annum is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   One year's interest. 
4,800 ÷ 4 = ₹1,200 
 Step 2   Now a single year's formula gives P. 
P × 16 × 1 / 100 = 1,200   ∴  P = ₹7,500

questions.question: In what time will a sum of money double itself at 6¼ % per annum simple interest? 6¼% Ů
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write the doubling condition. 
P × (25/4) × t / 100 = P 
 Step 2   Cancel P and solve. 
t = 100 ÷ (25/4) = 16 years

questions.question: S deposits a total of ₹50000 in two accounts which give simple interest at the rate of 8% and 12% per annum respectively. After one year he receives a total of 5200 as interest. How much money does he deposit in his account with 12% interest rate? S
questions.solution:
Step 1   Find the overall rate the ₹5,200 
represents. 
5,200 / 50,000 × 100 = 10.4% 
 Step 2   Put 8% and 12% on either side of 10.4%. 
distances 10.4 − 8 = 2.4  and  12 − 10.4 = 1.6   ⇒  
parts = 1.6 : 2.4 = 2 : 3 
 Step 3   The 12% account takes the 3 parts. 
(3/5) × 50,000 = ₹30,000

questions.question: The difference between the simple interest on a fixed amount for 7 years and on the same amount for 12 years is ₹2,500. If the rate of interest is 10% p.a., then the amount is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Convert both spans to percentages of P. 
7 × 10% = 70%        12 × 10% = 120% 
 Step 2   Their gap is the given ₹2,500. 
50% of P = 2,500   ∴  P = ₹5,000

questions.question: What is the simple interest on a sum of ₹99000 at 12½% per annum for a period of 9 months? ₹99000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Rewrite the rate and the time. 
12½% = 1/8        9 months = 9/12 year 
 Step 2   Multiply straight through. 
SI = 99,000 × (1/8) × (9/12) = ₹9,281.25

questions.question: A person invested one-fourth of the sum of ₹25,000 at a certain rate of simple interest and the rest at 4% p.a. higher rate. If the total interest received for 2 years is ₹4,125, what is the rate at which the second sum was invested?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Split the sum. 
one-fourth = ₹6,250 at x%,   the rest = ₹18,750 
at (x + 4)%,  both for 2 years 
 Step 2   Add the two interests to ₹4,125. 
125x + 375(x + 4) = 4,125   ⇒  500x = 2,625   ∴  x = 
5.25 
 Step 3   Read the question again — it asks for the 
SECOND rate. 
x + 4 = 9.25%

questions.question: If the annual rate of simple interest increases from 11% to 17½% then a person's yearly income increases by 1,071.20. The simple interest (in ₹) on the same sum at 10% for 5 years is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Find the rate difference and recover P. 
17½% − 11% = 6.5% of P = 1,071.20   ∴  P = ₹16,480 
 Step 2   10% for 5 years is simply half the sum. 
SI = 50% of 16,480 = ₹8,240

questions.question: Two equal sums are borrowed at 10% and 8% simple interest p.a. respectively, at the same time. The first sum is received 2 years earlier than the second one and the amount received in each case was ₹36,900. Each sum was ____?
questions.solution:
Step 1   The first sum is received 2 years earlier. 
10t = 8(t + 2)   ⇒  2t = 16   ∴  t = 8 years 
 Step 2   Use the amount on the 10% sum. 
P(1 + 80/100) = 36,900   ⇒  1.8 P = 36,900   ∴  P = 
₹20,500

questions.question: If the total simple interest on a sum of ₹1,400 for 4 years at rate of interest x% p.a. and on the same sum for two years at the same rate, is ₹672, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write both interests. 
1400 · x · 4/100 + 1400 · x · 2/100 = 672 
 Step 2   Combine and solve. 
56x + 28x = 84x = 672   ∴  x = 8

questions.question: A sum of ₹2400 is invested for 4 years at R% per annum, simple interest and the simple interest received is ₹1152. Find the amount received after 3 years when the same sum is invested at (R + 8)% p.a., simple interest. ₹2400
questions.solution:
Step 1   One year's interest, then the rate. 
1,152 ÷ 4 = ₹288 a year   ⇒  R = 288/2400 × 100 
= 12% 
 Step 2   New rate R + 8 = 20%, i.e. one-fifth. 
yearly interest = 2,400 ÷ 5 = ₹480 
 Step 3   Three years of it. 
480 × 3 = ₹1,440
